pages-B.notes: Checked and found fine (group B pages): Pakistan time handling (lib/time.ts pktParts/pktTime/pktDate, slot labels by start time, day separators via dayBreaks/`date`, tooltips with absolute times; viewer money stripping honoured in SlotTable, Breakdown, Versions, Compare drawer with "Hidden for your role"); safeStatus bans optimal/guaranteed; plan polling 5 min + now-marker 60 s; versions list opens read-only earlier plans; held state (GET /plan -> {plan:null, held}) rendered by PlanHeld with pause/release vs guard wording and "Read the held plan"; time-limited note (solver.time_limited, mip_gap, time_limit_s), threshold_repair and shed_rule_resolve notes, relaxed_retry note, genset_state_unknown, charge-until (charge_end_ts) on slots and vendor intents; findings.title: POST /control/{action} and /plan/apply take unvalidated dicts: a non-numeric hours or soc_pct answers 500 instead of a 422 refusal
findings.label: bug
findings.steps: As an operator: POST /api/sites/<id>/control/hold with body {"hours": "four"} (or {"soc_pct": "abc"}, or {"hours": {}}). `float(inp.get("hours", 4) or 4)` on line 154 and `float(inp.get("soc_pct") ...)` on line 161 raise ValueError/TypeError, which no route-level handler catches; api.py's catch-all (line 317-321) turns it into 500 'The server could not answer this request'. Same shape on POST /plan/apply (line 94: raw dict, `str(inp.get("day"))[:10]` accepts any junk as the day_local key that control_state later matches against today).
findings.expected: HANDOFF §4 'Strict models: request models forbid unknown fields. A refusal is a Refusal(status, sentence, code)'; plan Part 2.8 untrusted input; the page expects a one-sentence 422 it can show in the dialog (control-actions.tsx line 100).
findings.actual: A malformed body is a 500 server fault with a request id, logged as a crash; unknown fields are silently accepted; `day` is stored unvalidated (e.g. 'yesterday' or '2026-13-45').
findings.evidence: routes_plans.py:152-168 (`inp: dict = Body(default={})`, float() calls); routes_plans.py:94-103; api.py:317-321 generic except -> 500. Contrast sites.OverrideFields (sites.py:366-370) which is a Strict model, and routes_sites.overrides_post which uses it.

findings.title: Advisory tier: the 'table to key in' is re-compiled every 15 minutes, so the installer's keyed table is a moving target and no daily table / write budget exists as Part 7.1 step 7 requires
findings.label: feature-gap
findings.area: Control: vendor table / Mark as applied
findings.steps: At an advisory_writes site (e.g. the demo textile plant), open /sites/:id/control, copy the table, mark it applied for today. Wait for the next tick (15 min; or press Re-solve now). Reload Control: `comp = plans.current(site_id)['slots']` now shows the new plan's table (different boundaries after a forecast update), the header still reads 'Following plan (table applied)' (control_state keys on any applied row for today), and nothing on the page says which table the installer actually keyed or that today's keyed table differs from the one shown.
findings.expected: Plan Part 7.1 step 7: 'the nightly table write after the 23:00 solve; an event rewrite only when the expected rupee gain exceeds a threshold (default Rs 500), the budget allows and the previous write is more than 60 minutes old'; Part 7.6: the installer keys the day's table and the product confirms that table from telemetry; UI-15 'the capabilities card with budgets used today'. The installer needs one stable daily table (plus an explicit 'a better table is worth Rs X, re-key?' nudge).
findings.actual: delivery.compile_mode_a is run on every tick and the control page always shows the current plan's table; `budget.used_today` counts plan_messages rows, which are written only on an edge key pull (routes_edge.py:410-427), so at a keyed-table site it is always '0 of 3' and never enforced; the applied log links a plan_id but the page never shows that plan's table against the current one. The tracker marks DLV-01 (write budget, 60-minute spacing) as [~].
findings.evidence: routes_plans.py:133-148 (control: `comp = (p or {}).get('slots')`, `writes_today` from plan_messages); routes_sites.py:47-52 (control_state 'following' on any applied row today); vendor-table.tsx:52-68 (days from control.compiled, table of the current plan); plans.py:391-470 (every tick compiles and stores slots; no budget logic); EMS_BUILD_PROGRESS.md:185 DLV-01 [~].

findings.title: grid_cap_w (the MDI cap) is dropped from every vendor layout, yet the twin enforces it: a keyed Deye/Growatt/Sungrow table cannot peak-shave, and `mdi_not_enforceable` is never reported
findings.label: spec-mismatch
findings.area: Control: vendor table / Mode A compiler
findings.steps: Site with a Deye inverter and an MDI tariff (demo Karachi feed mill). GET /sites/:id/control: each compiled slot carries `grid_cap_w` (delivery.py:193-196) and the twin honours it (twin.py:213-214, 296), so the wrong-plan guard, the compare drawer and the advisory confirmation all simulate a device that caps grid import. vendor_view (delivery.py:219-227) emits program/time/power_w/soc_pct/grid_charge/gen_charge for Deye and slot/start/end/mode/soc_pct for the rest: no grid cap, and `max_discharge_w` is the plan's max discharge (line 170), not `max(0, Lhi - mdi_cap_kw)`.
findings.expected: Plan Part 7.1 step 4: on Deye, Growatt and Sungrow (no peak-shaving primitive) set each peak-risk slot's max_discharge_w to at least max(0, Lhi - mdi_cap_kw) and the floor so that energy is available; where the brand cannot hold both, 'the expected MDI rise is reported on the plan as mdi_not_enforceable, so the savings page never credits a peak cut the device could not make'.
findings.actual: The keyed table has no cap at all; the plan's summary never carries mdi_not_enforceable; the compare drawer and savings MDI lever assume a cap the installer cannot key. DESIGN_LOG (v1 build) says 'every slot carries grid_cap_w (the plan's MDI cap) so the device peak-shaves to it', which only holds for an edge that reads grid_cap_w, not for Part 7.6's installer-keyed delivery, which is the only delivery in v1.
findings.evidence: delivery.py:170-171, 182-196, 212-228; twin.py:200-214, 296; DESIGN_LOG 'Mode A compiler (Part 7.1)' bullet; BRANDS[deye].mdi_primitive False (delivery.py:29-30).

findings.title: Huawei vendor view emits a 'hold' value in charge_or_discharge, which the Huawei TOU table cannot take; the global cut-off and floor registers Part 7.1 requires are absent
findings.label: spec-mismatch
findings.steps: Site with inverter brand huawei and a plan with a hold slot (any hold_for_outage step). GET /sites/:id/control -> vendor_view rows: {period, start, end, charge_or_discharge: 'hold'}. The control page shows 'Hold' under 'Charge or discharge'.
findings.expected: Plan Part 7.1 step 4: Huawei is translated to 'one global grid-charge cut-off (the maximum of the grid-charge targets) with floors through the discharge and backup SoC registers'; Huawei's TOU periods only carry Charge or Discharge (R8 2.15: 'Start, End, Charge or Discharge, Days, plus the working-mode value'). A hold has to be expressed as a discharge floor, not a third period type.
findings.actual: vendor_view maps hold -> 'hold' (line 224-225), gives no cut-off SoC, no discharge/backup floor and no Days mask, so an installer cannot key the row as shown.
findings.evidence: delivery.py:223-225; BRANDS[huawei].fields ['start','end','charge_or_discharge'] (delivery.py:31-32); vendor-table.tsx:21-23 maps charge_or_discharge through modeWords.

findings.title: Growatt, Sungrow, Voltronic, Solis and 'other' all get the same generic slot/start/end/mode/soc_pct rows, not the vendor's layout, and their rows do not match the grammar's declared fields
findings.label: feature-gap
findings.steps: Set the inverter brand to growatt (or sungrow, voltronic, solis). GET /sites/:id/control: grammar.fields says ['start','end','enabled'] / ['start','end','target_soc'] / ['mode'] / ['start','end','current_a'], but vendor_view (line 226-227) returns {slot, start, end, mode, soc_pct} for every one of them. The page draws columns from the row keys (vendor-table.tsx:28-32), so the installer sees a generic table titled with the brand's layout ('three charge and three discharge windows').
findings.expected: Plan Part 9.3 UI-15 'the Mode A table in the vendor's layout per brand'; R8 2.15: Growatt SPH 3 battery-first and 3 grid-first windows with begin, end, enable and the global rates and SoC limits; Sungrow and Voltronic the emulated slot list with the EMS mode / POP and PCP values; Solis charge/discharge slots with current.
findings.actual: Only Deye and Huawei have brand rows; Sungrow's target_soc is never emitted (rows carry the floor as soc_pct); Growatt max_slots is 3 total while the plan and the grammar's own layout text say 3 charge + 3 discharge (6).
findings.evidence: delivery.py:28-43 (BRANDS fields vs layout), 212-228 (vendor_view); vendor-table.tsx:28-32 vendorColumns; slots-view.tsx:26 prints 'three charge and three discharge windows, up to 3 slots a day' for Growatt.

findings.title: Write-budget counter compares a UTC timestamp with a Karachi date
findings.label: bug
findings.steps: Closed-loop site whose edge pulls the plan between 00:00 and 05:00 PKT (19:00-24:00 UTC of the previous day). GET /sites/:id/control -> budget.used_today.
findings.expected: Writes counted per Karachi day (the day the page and the brand's daily budget mean).
findings.actual: `substr(sent_at,1,10) = today().isoformat()` compares store._now() (UTC ISO, store.py:106-107) with routes_common.today() (PKT date, routes_common.py:65-66), so pulls in the first five hours of a PKT day are counted on the previous day and the last five UTC hours' pulls are missed.
findings.evidence: routes_plans.py:141-142; store.py:106; routes_common.py:65.

findings.title: Plan Table view has no override glyphs and no past-24-hour actuals, although the tracker marks UI-09 done with both
findings.label: feature-gap
findings.steps: Place a Hold on Control, open /sites/:id/plan?view=table. The plan summary carries `overrides` (plans.py:229, 415) and the steps' reason may be operator_hold, but no row shows a glyph for the override window; scroll up: there are no past rows with measured values, only the plan's own steps greyed where `slotPast`.
findings.expected: Plan Part 9.3 UI-09: 'Table (SlotTable with the reason column and override glyphs, past 24 hours greyed with actuals)'; R8 2.9 Flags column (manual override glyph, clamped, budget-limited) and 'the past 24 hours available by scrolling up, greyed, with actuals beside plan'; EMS_BUILD_PROGRESS UI-09 [x] 'the SlotTable with the reason column, override glyphs and past actuals'.

findings.evidence: slot-table.tsx:15-78; plan-views.tsx:40-46; types/api.ts PlanSummary.overrides: unknown[]; EMS_BUILD_PROGRESS.md:157.

findings.title: No 'it took / it did not take' card: a keyed table is confirmed only by the nightly job, not 30 minutes after the first peak slot
findings.label: feature-gap
findings.steps: Advisory site: mark today's table applied at 10:00; the evening discharge slot starts 18:30. Watch the applied log and the control chip until midnight: confirmation stays 'pending' and fidelity '–'; it changes only after nightly_company (00:40 PKT) runs verify.compute_day(yesterday) which calls confirm_applied.
findings.expected: Plan Part 9.5: 'an "it took" or "it did not take" card 30 minutes after the first peak slot'; Part 7.6 confirms 'discharge rises above 10 percent of rated within 30 minutes of a peak-slot start'; tracker UI-20 [x] names the 'it took' card.
findings.actual: confirm_applied is reached only from verify.compute_day (verify.py:725) in the nightly job (scheduler.py:50-52); the frontend has no such card (no component mentions it); the mark-applied dialog promises 'The site's behaviour then confirms it (or not) after the first peak slot' (mark-applied.tsx:56), which is not what happens.
findings.evidence: scheduler.py:38-52; verify.py:705-727; mark-applied.tsx:56, 84; EMS_BUILD_PROGRESS.md:158.

findings.title: Tier sign-off is not shown on Devices and control although the docs say it is
findings.label: feature-gap
findings.steps: Change a site's tier in Site settings with a sign-off, open /sites/:id/control. The capabilities card lists tier now / capable / allowed but no sign-off line (who, when, wording).
findings.expected: docs/BACKEND_ASKS.md 'Tier sign-off record (tier_signoff in GET /api/sites/:id): shown on Site settings, Control (round 4)'; backend HANDOFF 8.B says the tier sign-off was wired; R8 2.15 lists the conformance/sign-off facts on the capabilities card.

findings.evidence: grep of frontend/src for tier_signoff: only sites/settings/tier-card.tsx and sites/onboarding/use-settle.ts; capabilities-card.tsx:34-44.

findings.title: After a CSV upload the chart, data-quality strip and imports log do not refresh (wrong query keys invalidated)
findings.label: bug
findings.steps: On /sites/:id/telemetry choose a custom range covering the file's days, upload a CSV. The green result notice appears, but the chart above keeps 'No data in this range', the Data quality card still says 'No CSV has been uploaded' and the Imports table is empty until the 5-minute poll or a reload.
findings.expected: The page's own data (qk.telemetry, qk.qualityAll, qk.heatmap) re-read after an import, as the control page does after an action.
findings.actual: onSuccess invalidates only `qk.site(siteId)`; keys.ts says qk.site(id) is a prefix of the site's queries, but qk.site(id) = ['gl','site',id] is only a prefix if invalidateQueries is called with that exact array — check: qk.telemetry = ['gl','site',id,'telemetry',q], which IS under the prefix, yet `useQuery` for telemetry has `enabled: !problem` and placeholderData, so a custom-range query refetches; the quality query (refetchInterval 5 min) is also under the prefix. If the prefix invalidation does reach them this finding reduces to: the Devices page's 14-day quality and the heatmap (staleTime 15 min) refetch, but the chart's dataset for a *preset* range ending now never includes historical rows anyway. Reported at low severity and 0.5 confidence because it depends on React Query prefix matching of qk.site.
findings.evidence: csv-upload.tsx:48-51; keys.ts:32-43; telemetry-page.tsx:62-74.

findings.title: Data-quality colour thresholds differ between the Telemetry page and the Devices page for the same figure
findings.label: ux
findings.steps: A day with 70 % completeness: on /telemetry it is red ('Green from 95 %, amber from 80 %, red below', data-quality.tsx:19-20, 35); on /devices the same day is amber (tone(): amber from 50 %).
findings.expected: One rule for the same quality measure across pages (plan Part 9.7 'one colour per ... in every chart, chip and node').
findings.actual: telemetry/data-quality.tsx uses 0.95/0.8; devices/data-quality-card.tsx uses 0.95/0.5.
findings.evidence: data-quality.tsx:19-20 vs data-quality-card.tsx:22.

findings.title: Plan checklist treats only site_type 'farm' as off-grid; a non-farm off-grid site is told to add a grid connection forever
findings.label: bug
findings.steps: Create an off-grid site of type other than farm (data.off_grid = true, no connection), before its first plan. /sites/:id/plan shows 'Add the grid connection and tariff: To do' with a link to the tariff tab.
findings.expected: DESIGN_LOG round 3: `SiteFields` carries `off_grid`; activate counts `data.off_grid`; the checklist should key on it.
findings.actual: `site?.data.site_type === "farm"` is used as the off-grid proxy; Site.data.off_grid (types/api.ts:272) is ignored.
findings.evidence: plan-empty.tsx:11; types/api.ts:272; sites.py:75.

findings.title: Mode A fallback block carries a 3-hour revert timer and lacks native_settings_ref / max_export_w_floor; the plan says Mode A has no revert timer
findings.label: spec-mismatch
findings.area: Plan Slots view and Control fallback card
findings.steps: GET /sites/:id/plan -> slots.fallback = {on_expiry: inverter_native, min_soc_floor_pct, revert_after_hours: 3}. The Slots view and the Fallback card say 'If the plan expires, or no fresh plan arrives for 3 h, the inverter returns to its native settings'.
findings.expected: Part 7.1 step 6: 'The Mode A fallback block carries on_expiry: inverter_native, min_soc_floor_pct, max_export_w_floor and native_settings_ref and no revert timer; the 1,800-second revert belongs to Mode B's volatile setpoints.' (Part 7.1's opening sentence also mentions a 3-hour revert, so the plan is internally inconsistent; step 6 is the operative rule for a persisted Deye/Growatt table.)
findings.actual: FALLBACK_HOURS = 3 is emitted for Mode A and shown to installers as a behaviour a keyed table does not have; the native capture version it falls back to is not referenced.
findings.evidence: delivery.py:44, 199-200; slot-words.ts:24-27 fallbackSentence; control-cards.tsx:11-18.

findings.title: Compare drawer silently compares against an assumed self-use baseline when no native capture exists
findings.label: ux
findings.steps: Site with a battery and a plan but no native capture (common at monitor before capture). Open 'Compare with native': the table shows figures for 'Native settings' with the method note 'the native arm the captured native settings'.
findings.expected: R8 2.9: the Compare drawer is 'disabled with "Needs the native-settings capture and 1 day of data"' until the capture exists; UI-12 blocks savings on the same condition.
findings.actual: routes_plans.plan_compare only checks for a battery; twin.native_policy falls back to self_use with a 20 % backup floor (twin.py:167) and the page labels it 'Native settings' / 'captured native settings' with no warning.
findings.evidence: routes_plans.py:109-112; twin.py:156-170; compare-drawer.tsx:39-41, 69-72.

findings.title: Release dialog says the plan 'keeps solving as a recommendation'; the backend stores it as held, which the Plan page then says
findings.label: ux
findings.steps: Press Release to native; the dialog text: 'The inverter runs on its own native settings until the release ends; the plan keeps solving as a recommendation.' Then open the Plan page: 'no plan is in force; the optimiser still solves every 15 minutes and keeps each plan for reading, marked held'.
findings.expected: One wording for one state (DESIGN_LOG rounds 1-2: under a release 'a tick stores its plan as held ... no plan is in force').
findings.actual: Two different descriptions of the same state across the two pages; 'recommendation' is the monitor-tier word (plan Part 9.4), which a release is not.
findings.evidence: control-actions.tsx:31-34 vs plan-held.tsx:45-49; plans.py:452-455.

findings.title: Per-step cost column rounds to whole rupees, so most 15-minute steps read 'Rs 0'
findings.label: ux
findings.steps: Admin at a site whose steps cost under Rs 50 each (a 100 kW site at Rs 30/kWh is Rs 750 per step, but off-peak battery or PV-covered steps are a few rupees): the Cost column shows 'Rs 0' or 'Rs 3' for values the API sends with two decimals.
findings.expected: R8 2.21: 'No decimals above Rs 1,000', implying decimals below it; Predbat-style per-slot costs need resolution to be readable.

findings.title: Telemetry series picker lacks half of the contract's series (grid import/export energy, battery voltage/current, genset running flag, inverter mode)

The minute table (telemetry.CSV_COLUMNS/NUMERIC) also stores grid_import_wh, grid_export_wh, battery_voltage_v, battery_current_a, genset_running, grid_frequency_hz, battery_soc_sigma_pct, which the API would serve.
findings.expected: Plan 9.3 UI-05 'Any series at 1 minute over any range'; R8 2.5 lists PV, load, battery (power, SoC BMS, SoC estimate with sigma band, voltage, current, temperature), grid (import, export, present, voltage, frequency), genset (running, kW, fuel, tank).
findings.actual: Only the 11 SERIES entries can be drawn; no 'today'/'yesterday' presets either (R8 2.5).

pages-A.notes:
Dimension: spec vs build for Fleet, site Overview, onboarding wizard, Site settings, Company settings, Account, sign-in/session, shell/navigation, founder console. Read: backend HANDOFF (4,5,7,8,9), DESIGN_LOG (all), EMS_BUILD_PLAN Part 9 (9.1-9.8), R8 sections 2.0-2.4, 2.17-2.21, frontend docs (HANDOFF, API_CONTRACT, BACKEND_ASKS, GATES), all source under features/{sites,overview,org,auth,ops}, components/layout, components/gates, components/ui (query-state, kpi-tile, empty-state), components/charts (energy-flow, reason-chip, spark-bars), lib/{format,time,use-meta,wording}, types/api.ts, lib/api/{endpoints,keys}.ts, and the backend's routes_sites.py (meta, control_state, fleet_row, site_now, overview_chart), scheduler.py, auth.py PERMISSIONS, money.py MONEY_KEYS, demo.py, routes_local.py, routes_founder.py, store_members.py, optimise.wear_cost. Nothing was run or modified.

Checked and found fine: banned words (safeStatus regex on plan status; no "optimal/guaranteed/maximum savings" in any group-A page text); last-data stamp on every site page (SiteLayout -> SiteHeader -> LastDataStamp, amber 5 min / red 30 min, Karachi tooltip) and per row on Fleet; viewer money: Fleet and Overview use KpiTile hidden="Hidden for your role" when the server strips *_rs, battery replacement cost and genset Rs fields show HiddenForRole for roles without see_costs, PriceVector shows "not available for your role" on 403, Review tab hides wear cost; no money reaches a viewer from group-A code paths; roles said in words everywhere (SaveRow denied text, NotForRole, demo-tab, tier-card, danger-view, keys-tab, members-tab); role chip in top bar; "/" lands on the only site's overview; Home/one-site rule; DEMO ribbon on demo-site pages only (deliberate review-r3 decision, test documents it) with DemoChip on Fleet rows; demo loading gated by edit_sites, removal by edit_workspace, with confirmation; tier change admin-only with sign-off dialog, tiers above tier_capable disabled, no_capture warning; connection removal/idempotency/draft resume/discard/draft_taken handling match API_CONTRACT and backend; lettered tabs have resolving ARIA pairs, ?tab= in URL, B-Review locked until the site exists; drafts autosave 1.5 s; sign-in has no sign-up, safeNext guards open redirects, 429 wait, session-ended overlay keeps edits, company chooser, not-set-up page; founder console has its own session header, two-step login, lockout wait, 8-hour expiry; formats follow 9.7 (Rs 1,234,567, Rs x.xx/kWh, one decimal under 100, "L", "62 %", 24-hour Karachi); wear cost per kWh discharged in site-form matches optimise.wear_cost; site delete is a soft delete so the Remove-site wording is correct; phone short menu has Overview, Plan, Control, Alerts, Genset; 16 px gutters (px-4). Known, documented gaps I did not list as findings (BACKEND_ASKS / HANDOFF 8.C): no "Test connection" probe (self-attested grid-present checkbox instead), no write budget / fallback / plan expiry / genset policy on tab D, no map pin or SMS contact on tab A, no fuel-metering kind on tab B, no sessions list / notification preferences / profile edit on Account, no report schedules on Company settings, no per-site Members tab (backend has no per-site membership), no weather footer.

findings.title: Overview checklist promises a plan every 15 minutes for a site that was never activated
findings.label: bug
findings.steps: Add a site: save tabs A-D (inverter, connection, native capture) but do not press Activate on the Review tab (or close the browser before it). Open /sites/:id. Compare with backend scheduler.py:23 (`if s.get("status") not in ("active",): continue`) and sites.py:222 (a new site is created with status "observing").
findings.expected: Plan 9.3 UI-04: "no plan: a checklist to the missing wizard tab". For an observing site the missing step is activation, so the card should keep a "To do: Activate the site (Review tab)" item linking to /sites/new?site=<id>&tab=review (the status is in `n.site.status`).
findings.actual: Checklist() (lines 75-99) only checks inverter, connection and native capture; when all three are in it renders the Notice "No plan is in force yet. Everything the optimiser needs is in, and it solves every 15 minutes; the Plan page says how the latest solve went." The tick skips non-active sites, so no plan ever arrives and the person is told to wait.
findings.evidence: overview-page.tsx:76-79 items list has no status check; :81-86 the all-done Notice; :178 `!n.now_next && s && <Checklist site={s} />`. scheduler.py:23 ticks only status "active"; routes_sites.py:191 `sites.set_status(site_id, "active")` happens only in site_activate.

findings.title: "Ask your administrator for a new password" but an administrator cannot set one, force a first-sign-in change, or clear a lockout
findings.label: spec-mismatch
findings.steps: Open /login: the foot of the form says "Forgotten your password? Ask your company's administrator for a new one." Sign in as the company admin, open /settings?view=members: the row controls are a role select and Switch on/off only. grep the backend: routes_platform.py has no password route; the only password-setting route is POST /api/founder/users/{id}/password (routes_founder.py:17), founder-only. routes_local.py:48-49 locks an address for 15 minutes after five wrong tries and no route clears it.
findings.expected: Plan 9.3 (last paragraph): "until PLT-11 adds email, an admin issues a one-time password with a forced change on first sign-in and can clear a lockout, the founder console does the same across companies, and the 'Forgot password' text says to ask the company's admin".

findings.evidence: login-page.tsx:71 sentence; members-tab.tsx:94-118 row controls (role select, Switch on/off only); routes_founder.py:17 POST /api/founder/users/{id}/password; routes_local.py:48 `_locked` 15-minute lock; no `password` in routes_platform.py.
